html:
French Senegal was France's oldest colony in tropical Africa, centred on the town of Saint-Louis at the mouth of the Senegal River, founded in 1659. The map shows it in its 1880 snapshot, when France was pushing inland from the coast. The country today is Senegal.

For two centuries the French held only trading posts, Saint-Louis and the island of Goree, buying gum arabic and slaves. Governor Louis Faidherbe changed that from 1854. He conquered the river valley, founded the port of Dakar in 1857, raised African troops, the tirailleurs, and in 1857 stopped Umar Tall at the siege of Medine.

Groundnuts became the cash crop. A railway from Dakar to Saint-Louis opened in 1885, against the resistance of Lat Dior, ruler of Cayor, who was killed in 1886. Africans born in the towns of Saint-Louis, Goree, Rufisque and Dakar held French citizenship. Senegal became the core of French West Africa and independent in 1960.
